nodes.bodyText:
FSDPManagedNNModuleVariable is used to represent Modules wrapped with FSDP, with inlining we do not do such specialization
l
ooking at FSDPManagedNNModuleVariable i see the following message:
    """
    Tracing behavior: trace into submodules and treat them as Unspecialized, do not
    register parameters to the top-level, treat them as function inputs.

    Guards behavior: if 'skip_fsdp_guards', many guards that would be installed
    by a vanilla UnspecializedNNModuleVariable are simply dropped, on the basis
    that a user wrapping their model in FSDP(model) is already opting into a
    requirement to not modify internal model state, which would already break FSDP without
    compilation.
    """

There are two test that fails in test_dynamo_distributed, that related to FSDP.

test_fsdp_skip_guards. (more problematic)
there is a flag skip_fsdp_guards when set, it is expected that guards be ignored. But those are not ignored with inlining.

    Guards behavior: if 'skip_fsdp_guards', many guards that would be installed
    by a vanilla UnspecializedNNModuleVariable are simply dropped, on the basis
    that a user wrapping their model in FSDP(model) is already opting into a
    requirement to not modify internal model state, which would already break FSDP without
    compilation.

        Note: comptime prints the guards before the time they get installed or not installed, so in both cases
       (skip or no skip) the same guards get printed.  The difference is that in the skip case, they show up
       with a special 'guard source' which will cuase them to not be installed.  So all we check for is the expected
       guard source 'local_fsdp_module'.

  Eager FSDP already assumes (requires, but without enforcement) that users don't mutate their
  model parameters/structure after FSDP wrapping, because FSDP wouldn't notice or update its FlatParams.
  Due to (2), we skip guards on inner contents of fsdp_managed modules, by using FSDPNNModuleSource as the
   guard source.  This behavior is gated on config.skip_fsdp_guards.


fsdp_orig_params_as (sounds solvable)
We perform a check on use_orig_params during compilation on a flag, that we skip doing when we inline. we can still do the check my re-ordering the code as the following,

     ## Move this check before is_dynamic_nn_module
     if getattr(value, "_is_fsdp_managed_module", False):
            # we can't do this assert inside FSDP constructor,
            # since we don't know yet whether dynamo will be used
            assert getattr(
                value, "_fsdp_use_orig_params", False
            ), "Dynamo only supports FSDP with use_orig_params=True"

        if mutation_guard.is_dynamic_nn_module(value, self.tx.export):
            # created dynamically, don't specialize on it
            self.install_guards(GuardBuilder.TYPE_MATCH)
            result = UnspecializedNNModuleVariable(value, source=self.source)
            if not SideEffects.cls_supports_mutation_side_effects(type(value)):
                # don't allow STORE_ATTR mutation with custom __setattr__
                return result
            return self.tx.output.side_effects.track_object_existing(value, result)
        elif issubclass(
            value.__class__, torch.nn.parallel.distributed.DistributedDataParallel
        ):
            self.install_guards(GuardBuilder.TYPE_MATCH)
            return UnspecializedNNModuleVariable(value)
        elif getattr(value, "_is_fsdp_managed_module", False):
            # See note [Dynamo treats FSDP wrapped modules as UnspecializedNNModule]
            # in fully_sharded_data_parallel.py for more information

            # Note on FSDP guarding
            # 1. We expect FSDP wrapping mutates an nn module irreversably (no way to de-wrap).
            # 2. Eager FSDP already assumes (requires, but without enforcement) that users don't mutate their
            #    model parameters/structure after FSDP wrapping, because FSDP wouldn't notice or update its FlatParams.
            #
            # Due to (1), once we enter this path we expect not to go back nor have to guard on type
            # or _is_fsdp_managed_module.
            #
            # TODO(whc) We could add a guard on the opposite case, where a user compiled/ran
            # pre-FSDP-wrapped model, then wrapped, to ensure that we recompile with the FSDP handling.
            #
            # Due to (2), we skip guards on inner contents of fsdp_managed modules, by using FSDPNNModuleSource as the
            # guard source.  This behavior is gated on config.skip_fsdp_guards.
            #
            # ID_MATCH is required to disambiguate cases as simple as a unit test that constructs 2 models and wraps
            # them differently with different FSDP configs.  (test_dynamo_distributed.py -k test_fsdp_aot_eager)
            self.install_guards(GuardBuilder.TYPE_MATCH, GuardBuilder.ID_MATCH)
            return FSDPManagedNNModuleVariable(value, source=self.get_source())

🐛 Describe the bug
We had many dynamic recompilation related to AMP (float vs half}. It happens when we use TORCHDYNAMO_INLINE_INBUILT_NN_MODULES=1 /cc @chauhang @penguinwu @ezyang @bobrenjc93 @voznesenskym @EikanWang @jgong5 @Guobing-Chen @XiaobingSuper @zhuhaozhe @blzheng @wenzhe-nrv @jiayisunx @chenyang78 @kadeng @amjames @msaroufim @bdhirsh @anijain2305
    @torch.compile(dynamic=True)
    def forward(self,
                tgt,
                long_term_memory=None,
                short_term_memory=None,
                curr_id_emb=None,
                self_pos=None,
                size_2d=(30, 30)):

        # Self-attention
        _tgt = self.norm1(tgt)
        if not self.use_self_pos:
            self_pos = None
        q = k = self.with_pos_embed(_tgt, self_pos)
        v = _tgt
        if self.global_dilation > 1:
            k = k[::self.global_dilation,:,:]
            v = v[::self.global_dilation,:,:]
        tgt2 = self.self_attn(q, k, v)[0]

        tgt = tgt + self.droppath(tgt2)

        # Long Short-Term Attention
        _tgt = self.norm2(tgt)

        curr_QV = self.linear_QV(_tgt)
        curr_QV = torch.split(curr_QV, self.d_model, dim=2)
        curr_Q = curr_K = curr_QV[0]
        curr_V = curr_QV[1]

        if self.d_att is not None:
            curr_Q = self.linear_Qd(curr_Q)
        local_Q = seq_to_2d(curr_Q, size_2d)

        if curr_id_emb is not None:
            global_K, global_V = self.fuse_key_value_id(
                curr_K, curr_V, curr_id_emb)
            if self.d_att is not None:
                global_K = self.linear_Kd(global_K)
            local_K = seq_to_2d(global_K, size_2d)
            local_V = seq_to_2d(global_V, size_2d)

            if self.global_dilation>1 and self.memory_dilation:
                nhw,bs,ck = global_K.shape
                cv = global_V.shape[-1]
                # n = nhw // (size_2d[0] * size_2d[1])

                if self.conv_dilation:
                    unfold_K = global_K.permute(1,2,0).reshape(bs,ck,size_2d[0],size_2d[1])
                    unfold_V = global_V.permute(1,2,0).reshape(bs,cv,size_2d[0],size_2d[1])
                    global_K = self.dilation_conv_K(unfold_K).reshape(bs,ck,-1).permute(2,0,1)
                    global_V = self.dilation_conv_V(unfold_V).reshape(bs,cv,-1).permute(2,0,1)
                else:

                    unfold_V = global_V.view(size_2d[0],size_2d[1],bs,cv)
                    global_K = unfold_K[::d,::d,:,:].reshape(-1,bs,ck)
                    global_V = unfold_V[::d,::d,:,:].reshape(-1,bs,cv)
        else:

            local_K, local_V = short_term_memory
        
        
        if self.memory_dilation:
            tgt2 = self.long_term_attn(curr_Q, global_K, global_V)[0]
        else:
            if self.global_dilation>1:
                nhw,bs,ck = global_K.shape
                cv = global_V.shape[-1]
                n = nhw // (size_2d[0] * size_2d[1])
                d = self.global_dilation
                if self.conv_dilation:
                    unfold_K = global_K.permute(1,2,0).reshape(bs*n,ck,size_2d[0],size_2d[1])
                    unfold_V = global_V.permute(1,2,0).reshape(bs*n,cv,size_2d[0],size_2d[1])
                    dilated_K = self.dilation_conv_K(unfold_K).reshape(bs,ck,-1).permute(2,0,1)
                    dilated_V = self.dilation_conv_V(unfold_V).reshape(bs,cv,-1).permute(2,0,1)
                else:
                    unfold_K = global_K.view(n,size_2d[0],size_2d[1],bs,ck)
                    unfold_V = global_V.view(n,size_2d[0],size_2d[1],bs,cv)
                    dilated_K = unfold_K[:,::d,::d,:,:].reshape(-1,bs,ck)
                    dilated_V = unfold_V[:,::d,::d,:,:].reshape(-1,bs,cv)
            else:
                dilated_K,dilated_V = global_K,global_V
            tgt2 = self.long_term_attn(curr_Q, dilated_K, dilated_V)[0]

        tgt3 = self.short_term_attn(local_Q, local_K, local_V)[0]

        if self.droppath_lst:
            tgt = tgt + self.droppath(tgt2 + tgt3)
        else:
            tgt = tgt + self.lst_dropout(tgt2 + tgt3)

        # Feed-forward
        _tgt = self.norm3(tgt)

        tgt2 = self.linear2(self.activation(self.linear1(_tgt), size_2d))

        tgt = tgt + self.droppath(tgt2)

        return tgt, [[curr_K, curr_V], [global_K, global_V],
                     [local_K, local_V]]

🐛 Describe the bug
Let's say for some reason you have some guard code that is misimplemented and it's calling a function that doesn't exist. Will Dynamo compilation fail? No. Instead, this will happen:
W0605 17:24:08.994000 140266518349376 torch/_dynamo/convert_frame.py:744] [4/8] torch._dynamo hit config.cache_size_limit (8)
W0605 17:24:08.994000 140266518349376 torch/_dynamo/convert_frame.py:744] [4/8]    function: 'forward' ([redacted]:149)
W0605 17:24:08.994000 140266518349376 torch/_dynamo/convert_frame.py:744] [4/8]    last reason: name 'Trunc' is not defined
W0605 17:24:08.994000 140266518349376 torch/_dynamo/convert_frame.py:744] [4/8] To log all recompilation reasons, use TORCH_LOGS="recompiles".

This is dumb. If we're generating malformed guard code, I definitely don't want to find out about it because I hit my cache size limit. Just fail the entire compile process early.
@hyuen and co ran into this, but I've also seen it in a few other cases too

🐛 Describe the bug
Doing inference with ChatTTS model (https://huggingface.co/2Noise/ChatTTS) will trigger non-deterministic recompiles.
E.g., for the first 5 texts we do inference in the testing script (https://gist.github.com/shunting314/a904ad991a9893c0a7f3c6e190f7437e ), if no re-compile happens, we get around 2x speed up. But when recompiles happens, end2end latency is slower than eager.
When recomiples happens, here is the log for the failed guards: https://gist.github.com/shunting314/e4dbcaed70d743b059343b629fe1b568
The recompilation is quite non-deterministic. I've seen the following happens

no recompile
the first input triggers recompile
the third and fourth input triggers recompile

Error logs
.

# all-miniLM
# https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
import time

#Mean Pooling - Take attention mask into account for correct averaging
def mean_pooling(model_output, attention_mask):
    token_embeddings = model_output[0] #First element of model_output contains all token embeddings
    input_mask_expanded = attention_mask.unsqueeze(-1).expand(token_embeddings.size()).float()
    return torch.sum(token_embeddings * input_mask_expanded, 1) / torch.clamp(input_mask_expanded.sum(1), min=1e-9)


# Sentences we want sentence embeddings for
sentences = ['This is an example sentence', 'Each sentence is converted']

# Load model from HuggingFace Hub
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2')
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2')

# Tokenize sentences
encoded_input = tokenizer(sentences, padding=True, truncation=True, return_tensors='pt')

@torch.compile(fullgraph=True)
def do_work():
    # Compute token embeddings
    with torch.no_grad():
        model_output = model(**encoded_input)

    # Perform pooling
    sentence_embeddings = mean_pooling(model_output, encoded_input['attention_mask'])

    # Normalize embeddings
    sentence_embeddings = F.normalize(sentence_embeddings, p=2, dim=1)

do_work()

🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
Hi, is it possible to recompile with new configs when hitting a certain type of exception in previous attempt?
Here's an example from discussion with @BoyuanFeng and @Yuzhen11 on recent cudagraph support for some input mutation functions.
_inductor.config.cudagraph_support_input_mutation can be set True at beginning.  As long as it throws a certain exception type, we turn it off and retry.

We can try some aggressive settings at beginning and gradually fall back to something more conservative without starting over.  This can make those heavy internal workflows more robust.
Rule-based interface can be like a list of [(exception type 1, config mutation 1), ...]

Thank you!

 First, NT/PT2 stack should "lift" these symints as inputs to the fx graph (@bdhirsh )

We can enhance confidence in the pipeline order by validating the p2p ops are batched correctly. We can do a "fake run" of the schedule by mocking the fwd/bwd operations and also mocking batch_isend_irecv calls to just log what is executed without actually executing.
For interleaved 1f1b and looped bfs we currently test different combinations of num_stages, num_ranks, num_microbatches by validating the schedule only (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/test/distributed/pipelining/test_schedule.py#L557). But we should add another test that actually calls .step() on the schedule and mock the corresponding P2P communications from PipelineStage get_*_send_ops and get_*_recv_ops which makes sure each send/recv is accurately batched and paired.

The following torch.xpu ops are missing (were available for IPEX):

 torch.xpu.memory_allocated()
 torch.xpu.max_memory_allocated()
 torch.xpu.reset_peak_memory_stats()

These operations are used for example on Huggingface side:

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/fd3238b4b0e1af4fae4a293cbfd1251ead40cd29/src/transformers/trainer_utils.py#L55
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/fd3238b4b0e1af4fae4a293cbfd1251ead40cd29/src/transformers/trainer_utils.py#L60
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/fd3238b4b0e1af4fae4a293cbfd1251ead40cd29/src/transformers/trainer_utils.py#L539

🐛 Describe the bug
When compiled autograd is enabled and model contains operations preferring inputs in channels last format, gradient and parameters memory layouts are inconsistent:

parameter: contiguous (default)
gradient: channels last

Issue doesn't appear when layout optimization is disabled (TORCHINDUCTOR_LAYOUT_OPTIMIZATION=0).
Reproducer:
import torch
from torch._dynamo.utils import maybe_enable_compiled_autograd


class Model(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = torch.nn.Conv2d(
            3,
            10,
            kernel_size=7,
            stride=[2, 2],
            padding=[3, 3],
            dilation=[1, 1],
            bias=False,
            groups=1,
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv1(x)
        return x


for compiled_autograd_enabled in [False, True]:
    input = torch.rand(16, 3, 224, 224)

    model_compiled = torch.compile(Model())
    with maybe_enable_compiled_autograd(compiled_autograd_enabled):
        out = model_compiled(input)
        loss = out.sum()
        loss.backward()

    param = next(model_compiled.parameters())
    grad = param.grad
    print("> compiled_autograd_enabled", compiled_autograd_enabled)
    print("parameter contiguous={}, channels_last={}".format(param.is_contiguous(memory_format=torch.contiguous_format),
          param.is_contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)))
    print("grad contiguous={}, channels_last={}".format(grad.is_contiguous(memory_format=torch.contiguous_format),
          grad.is_contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)))
Output:
> compiled_autograd_enabled False
parameter contiguous=True, channels_last=False
grad contiguous=True, channels_last=False

> compiled_autograd_enabled True
parameter contiguous=True, channels_last=False
grad contiguous=False, channels_last=True

Output with TORCHINDUCTOR_LAYOUT_OPTIMIZATION=0:
> compiled_autograd_enabled False
parameter contiguous=True, channels_last=False
grad contiguous=True, channels_last=False

> compiled_autograd_enabled True
parameter contiguous=True, channels_last=False
grad contiguous=True, channels_last=False

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
Foreach kernel (especially those generated for the optimizer) is very large and takes quite some time to compile. The reason is we duplicate the main block of code to process each tensor's gradient update. Those code need to be repeatedly lowered and transformed in triton which takes time.
Here is one initial idea which does not ultimately work but can be a good step stone to think about. Instead of codegen duplicate code for each tensor, we only codegen the code that's specific to each tensor

xpid_offset
xnumel
in-ptrs
out-ptrs

And then we move the common code to a function and call this function for each tensor.
Unfortunately this does not work, since triton by default will inline every function call.
But based on this idea, we can do something like this:
    if xpid >= 0 and xpid < 1:
        # setup code for this group
        # e.g. setup pid range and in/out ptrs and assign them to placeholder variables.
        # Here shows an example
        xpid_offset = xpid - 0
        xnumel = 23440896
        i0 = in_ptr0
        i1 = in_ptr1
        i2 = in_ptr2
        i3 = in_ptr3
        i4 = in_ptr4
        o0 = out_ptr0
        o1 = out_ptr2
        o2 = out_ptr3
    elif xpid >= 1 and xpid < 577:
        # setup code for this group
     ...
    else:
         tl.device_assert(False, "can not reach here")

    # Common body that uses the placeholder variables.
    # here is some simplified example. Full example will be provided below
    xoffset = xpid_offset * XBLOCK
    xindex = xoffset + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)[:]
    xmask = xindex < xnumel
    x0 = xindex
    tmp0 = tl.load(i0 + (x0), xmask)
    tmp1 = tl.load(i1 + (x0), xmask)
    tmp6 = tl.load(i2 + (x0), xmask)
    tmp13 = tl.load(i3 + (x0), xmask)
    tmp15 = tl.load(i4 + (0))
    ....
    tl.store(o0 + (x0), tmp5, xmask)
    tl.store(o1 + (x0), tmp34, xmask)
    tl.store(o2 + (x0), tmp12, xmask)

The trick here is to codegen the 'setup code' for each branch in a way that 'parameters' are assigned to placeholder variables. Those placeholder variables work like parameter and will be used in the 'common body'.
Here is an example optimizer wrapper generated for BertForMaskedLM:
https://gist.github.com/shunting314/50343179d4cb9889526a34a2a00eb685#file-orig_wrapper-py-L1414
I manually apply the idea to triton_for_fused_2 kernel, and get https://gist.github.com/shunting314/e3396bd9753045313f90d829b42bc906#file-wrapper-py-L1414
The compilation time for triton_for_fused_2 improve from 4.574s to 0.613s (7.5x improvement).
cc @ezyang @msaroufim @bdhirsh @anijain2305 @chauhang @voznesenskym @penguinwu @EikanWang @jgong5 @Guobing-Chen @XiaobingSuper @zhuhaozhe @blzheng @wenzhe-nrv @jiayisunx @peterbell10 @ipiszy @yf225 @chenyang78 @kadeng @muchulee8 @ColinPeppler @amjames @desertfire @mlazos @janeyx99 @jansel @Chillee @eellison

🐛 Describe the bug
During the Inductor lowering process, downstream op X is not recognizing that its input tensor was mutated by an auto_functionalize'd op, and instead X just uses the pre-mutation version of the input tensor.
Repro:
import torch
from torch._decomp import register_decomposition

lib = torch.library.Library("fsdp_test", "DEF")

lib.define("chunk_cat_(Tensor(a!) ret, Tensor[] tensors, int dim, int num_chunks) -> ()")

@torch.library.impl(lib, "chunk_cat_", "Meta")
def chunk_cat_(ret, tensors, dim, num_chunks):
    torch._chunk_cat(
        tensors, dim, num_chunks, out=ret
    )

@torch.library.impl(lib, "chunk_cat_", "CUDA")
def chunk_cat_(ret, tensors, dim, num_chunks):
    torch._chunk_cat(tensors, dim, num_chunks, out=ret)


def f(x, y, z):
    full_default_3: "f32[2, 524544]" = torch.ops.aten.full.default([2, 524544], 1.0, dtype = torch.float32, layout = torch.strided, device = "cuda", pin_memory = False)
    chunk_cat_default_1 = torch.ops.fsdp_test.chunk_cat_.default(full_default_3, [x, y, z], 0, 2)
    mul_out = torch.mul(full_default_3, full_default_3)
    sum_out = mul_out.sum()
    return sum_out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    x = torch.randn([1024, 512], device="cuda")
    y = torch.randn([512], device="cuda")
    z = torch.randn([1024, 512], device="cuda")
    eager_out = f(x, y, z)

    compiled_aot_eager_f = torch.compile(f, backend="aot_eager", fullgraph=True)
    compiled_aot_eager_out = compiled_aot_eager_f(x, y, z)
    assert torch.allclose(eager_out, compiled_aot_eager_out), f"eager_out: {eager_out}, compiled_aot_eager_out: {compiled_aot_eager_out}"   # passes

    compiled_inductor_f = torch.compile(f, backend="inductor", fullgraph=True)
    compiled_inductor_out = compiled_inductor_f(x, y, z)
    assert torch.allclose(eager_out, compiled_inductor_out), f"eager_out: {eager_out}, compiled_inductor_out: {compiled_inductor_out}"  # fails
Inductor generated code is:
def call(args):
    arg0_1, arg1_1, arg2_1 = args
    args.clear()
    assert_size_stride(arg0_1, (1024, 512), (512, 1))
    assert_size_stride(arg1_1, (512, ), (1, ))
    assert_size_stride(arg2_1, (1024, 512), (512, 1))
    with torch.cuda._DeviceGuard(0):
        torch.cuda.set_device(0)
        buf0 = empty_strided_cuda((2, 524544), (524544, 1), torch.float32)
        # Source Nodes: [full_default_3], Original ATen: [aten.full]
        stream0 = get_raw_stream(0)
        triton_poi_fused_full_0.run(buf0, 1049088, grid=grid(1049088), stream=stream0)
        # Source Nodes: [full_default_3], Original ATen: [aten.full]
        buf1 = torch.ops.fsdp_test.chunk_cat_.default(buf0, [arg0_1, arg1_1, arg2_1], 0, 2)
        del arg0_1
        del arg1_1
        del arg2_1
        buf3 = empty_strided_cuda((129, ), (1, ), torch.float32)
        # Source Nodes: [full_default_3, mul_out, sum_out], Original ATen: [aten.full, aten.mul, aten.sum]
        triton_red_fused_full_mul_sum_1.run(buf3, 129, 8133, grid=grid(129), stream=stream0)
        del buf0
        buf4 = empty_strided_cuda((), (), torch.float32)
        # Source Nodes: [full_default_3, mul_out, sum_out], Original ATen: [aten.full, aten.mul, aten.sum]
        triton_per_fused_full_mul_sum_2.run(buf3, buf4, 1, 129, grid=grid(1), stream=stream0)
        del buf3
    return (buf4, )
Notice neither buf0 or buf1 (mutated tensor by chunk_cat_) is used downstream, which deviates from eager semantics.
Interestingly, @bdhirsh found that if we comment out the decompose_auto_functionalized() pass in 
  
    
      pytorch/torch/_inductor/fx_passes/post_grad.py
    
    
         Line 125
      in
      05fa05c
    
  
  
    

        
          
           decompose_auto_functionalized(gm.graph) 
        
    
  

, then this passes. @zou3519 commented that this can work, but auto_functionalized will clone all the mutated inputs, so it is not performant. Richard commented that Inductor is supposed to re-inplace it and remove the unnecessary clones, and that's what decompose_auto_functionalized is for.
@zou3519 confirmed that it's indeed a recent regression.
Versions
nightly

nodes.bodyText:
(reported by @yf225)
🐛 Describe the bug
During the Inductor lowering process, downstream op X is not recognizing that its input tensor was mutated by an auto_functionalize'd op, and instead X just uses the pre-mutation version of the input tensor.
Repro:
import torch
from torch._decomp import register_decomposition

lib = torch.library.Library("fsdp_test", "DEF")

lib.define("chunk_cat_(Tensor(a!) ret, Tensor[] tensors, int dim, int num_chunks) -> ()")

@torch.library.impl(lib, "chunk_cat_", "Meta")
def chunk_cat_(ret, tensors, dim, num_chunks):
    torch._chunk_cat(
        tensors, dim, num_chunks, out=ret
    )

@torch.library.impl(lib, "chunk_cat_", "CUDA")
def chunk_cat_(ret, tensors, dim, num_chunks):
    torch._chunk_cat(tensors, dim, num_chunks, out=ret)


def f(x, y, z):
    full_default_3: "f32[2, 524544]" = torch.ops.aten.full.default([2, 524544], 1.0, dtype = torch.float32, layout = torch.strided, device = "cuda", pin_memory = False)
    chunk_cat_default_1 = torch.ops.fsdp_test.chunk_cat_.default(full_default_3, [x, y, z], 0, 2)
    mul_out = torch.mul(full_default_3, full_default_3)
    sum_out = mul_out.sum()
    return sum_out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    x = torch.randn([1024, 512], device="cuda")
    y = torch.randn([512], device="cuda")
    z = torch.randn([1024, 512], device="cuda")
    eager_out = f(x, y, z)

    compiled_aot_eager_f = torch.compile(f, backend="aot_eager", fullgraph=True)
    compiled_aot_eager_out = compiled_aot_eager_f(x, y, z)
    assert torch.allclose(eager_out, compiled_aot_eager_out), f"eager_out: {eager_out}, compiled_aot_eager_out: {compiled_aot_eager_out}"   # passes

    compiled_inductor_f = torch.compile(f, backend="inductor", fullgraph=True)
    compiled_inductor_out = compiled_inductor_f(x, y, z)
    assert torch.allclose(eager_out, compiled_inductor_out), f"eager_out: {eager_out}, compiled_inductor_out: {compiled_inductor_out}"  # fails
Inductor generated code is:
def call(args):
    arg0_1, arg1_1, arg2_1 = args
    args.clear()
    assert_size_stride(arg0_1, (1024, 512), (512, 1))
    assert_size_stride(arg1_1, (512, ), (1, ))
    assert_size_stride(arg2_1, (1024, 512), (512, 1))
    with torch.cuda._DeviceGuard(0):
        torch.cuda.set_device(0)
        buf0 = empty_strided_cuda((2, 524544), (524544, 1), torch.float32)
        # Source Nodes: [full_default_3], Original ATen: [aten.full]
        stream0 = get_raw_stream(0)
        triton_poi_fused_full_0.run(buf0, 1049088, grid=grid(1049088), stream=stream0)
        # Source Nodes: [full_default_3], Original ATen: [aten.full]
        buf1 = torch.ops.fsdp_test.chunk_cat_.default(buf0, [arg0_1, arg1_1, arg2_1], 0, 2)
        del arg0_1
        del arg1_1
        del arg2_1
        buf3 = empty_strided_cuda((129, ), (1, ), torch.float32)
        # Source Nodes: [full_default_3, mul_out, sum_out], Original ATen: [aten.full, aten.mul, aten.sum]
        triton_red_fused_full_mul_sum_1.run(buf3, 129, 8133, grid=grid(129), stream=stream0)
        del buf0
        buf4 = empty_strided_cuda((), (), torch.float32)
        # Source Nodes: [full_default_3, mul_out, sum_out], Original ATen: [aten.full, aten.mul, aten.sum]
        triton_per_fused_full_mul_sum_2.run(buf3, buf4, 1, 129, grid=grid(1), stream=stream0)
        del buf3
    return (buf4, )
Notice neither buf0 or buf1 (mutated tensor by chunk_cat_) is used downstream, which deviates from eager semantics.
Interestingly, @bdhirsh found that if we comment out the decompose_auto_functionalized() pass in 
  
    
      pytorch/torch/_inductor/fx_passes/post_grad.py
    
    
         Line 125
      in
      05fa05c
    
  
  
    

        
          
           decompose_auto_functionalized(gm.graph) 
        
    
  

, then this passes. @zou3519 commented that this can work, but auto_functionalized will clone all the mutated inputs, so it is not performant. Richard commented that Inductor is supposed to re-inplace it and remove the unnecessary clones, and that's what decompose_auto_functionalized is for.
@zou3519 confirmed that it's indeed a recent regression.
Versions
nightly

def check_module_importable(module, max_length, lock):
    proc = subprocess.run(

        timeout=10.0,
        capture_output=True,
        check=False,
    )

    return proc.returncode


def main():
    os.chdir(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(torch.__file__)))

    submodules = [
        path.removesuffix('.py').removesuffix('/__init__').replace('/', '.')
        for path in glob.iglob('torch/**/*.py', recursive=True)
    ]

    modules = sorted(
        set(
            itertools.chain.from_iterable(
                itertools.accumulate(mod.split('.'), lambda p, x: f'{p}.{x}') for mod in submodules
            )
        )
    )

    max_length = max(len(mod) for mod in modules)
    lock = threading.Lock()

    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
        return_codes = list(
            executor.map(
                check_module_importable,
                modules,
                itertools.repeat(max_length),
                itertools.repeat(lock),
            )
        )

    if any(return_codes):
        failed_imports = [mod for mod, return_code in zip(modules, return_codes) if return_code]
        print()
        print('>' * (max_length + 18))
        print(f'Failed to import {len(failed_imports)} module(s):')
        for mod in failed_imports:
            print(f'  {mod}')
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
Hi,
Recently, I found that the different ways to define the trainable parameter might cause different training results, even under the same seed.
My question is: what is the difference between way 1 and way 2? Here are definitions of way 1 and way 2:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Way1(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(Way1, self).__init__()
        self.wh = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros((10, 10)), requires_grad=True)
        nn.init.xavier_normal_(self.wh)


class Way2(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, device):
        super(Way2, self).__init__()
        self.device = device
        self.wh = self.init_weight((10, 10))

    def init_weight(self, shape):
        _para = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(shape), requires_grad=True).to(self.device)
        nn.init.xavier_normal_(_para)
        return _para


if __name__ == '__main__':
    w = Way1()
    for name, param in w.named_parameters():
        print('w1', name, param)

    w2 = Way2('cuda:0').to('cuda:0')
    for name, param in w2.named_parameters():
        print('w2', name, param)
I found that initing the trainable parameters in way 1 seems to get a smaller loss than that in way 2. Is it true that if we create an optimizer with net.parameters() and call optimizer.step(), the self.wh in way1 will be automatically optimized and that in way2 will not?
I would greatly appreciate any insights that point this out for me. :)
